title: The impact of probiotics or synbiotics on individuals with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM): a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (T1DM) is a chronic autoimmune condition characterized by insulin deficiency. Probiotics and synbiotics are believed to impact glycemic control. This study aims to evaluate their effects on individuals with T1DM.

title: Metabolic, enzymatic, and probiotic profiling of Lactococcus lactis LBM15: inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus biofilm and virulence genes, and GPR-based prediction.
abstract: This study characterized a Lactococcus lactis strain (LBM15) isolated from traditional yogurt and evaluated its probiotic, antimicrobial, and anti-biofilm attributes, along with its physiological robustness and safety-associated characteristics. The isolate was identified by 16S rRNA sequencing (99% similarity) and exhibited a carbohydrate utilization pattern typical of dairy L. lactis, including efficient fermentation of common hexoses and β-glucosides. title: Surface-functionalized Bifidobacterium bifidum alleviates Clostridioides difficile infection by coordinating host immune modulation and gut microbiota restoration☆.
abstract: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) is a major ecological disruption of the gut ecosystem, characterized by loss of colonization resistance, persistent inflammatory feedback and incomplete microbial recovery. Meta-analysis of clinical cohorts identified Bifidobacterium depletion as a conserved feature of CDI-associated dysbiosis, suggesting that restoring this genus may promote recovery from CDI. Comparative in vitro assays identified B. bifidum as the most protective strain. This effect wa...

title: Safety Assessment of Spirulina Intake on Cytochrome P450 3A-Mediated Drug Metabolism: A Comprehensive Study from an In Vitro Study to a Human Clinical Trial.
abstract: Spirulina has been gaining increasing attention as a dietary supplement, yet its potential to induce food-drug interactions when taken alongside medications remains insufficiently understood. Inhibition of cytochrome P450 3A (CYP3A), a major drug-metabolizing enzyme, is of concern, as it may play a key role in adverse effect development. Therefore, we aimed to determine whether spirulina induces food-drug interactions through CYP3A inhibition. To assess the inhibitory effects of spirulina on CYP...
journal: Journal of nutritional science and vitaminology

title: Effects of Saccharomyces cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 and vitamin K2 on the gut microbiota of patients with osteoporosis and healthy controls using in vitro short-term colonic simulations.
abstract: The gut microbiome may be involved in bone health through the gut-bone axis. Saccharomyces cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 benefits gut health in patients with irritable bowel syndrome, which is more prevalent in women and may be associated with higher osteoporosis prevalence. We evaluated the effects of S. cerevisiae CNCM I-3856 ± vitamin K2 (K2) on the gut microbiota of patients with osteoporosis and healthy controls. Short-term in vitro colonic fermentations were performed using feces from healthy and...

title: Early post-weaning probiotic supplementation alters gut microbial community structure and predicted metabolic function in female juvenile mice.
abstract: To characterize the effects of early post-weaning multi-strain probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition, predicted metabolic function, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles in female juvenile mice at the pubertal window.

title: Effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices and oxidative-stress biomarkers in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and dose-response analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Diabetes and metabolic syndrome are major public health challenges closely linked to oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired insulin signaling. Selenium, an essential trace element with antioxidant and immunomodulatory roles, has been proposed as an adjunctive strategy for metabolic regulation; however, evidence from randomized trials remains inconsistent. We evaluated the effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices, oxidative-stress-related biomarkers, lipid metabolism, and rel...

title: Effects of a Saccharomyces uvarum Cell-Based Preparation on Gut Microbial Ecology and Metabolic Activity in Adults Without Diagnosed Gastrointestinal Disease: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Crossover Pilot Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Yeast-based probiotic candidates are increasingly investigated as potential modulators of gut ecology, although evidence in healthy individuals remains limited. This randomized, single-blind, crossover study primarily evaluated the tolerability of ATECREM Serius containing Saccharomyces uvarum SERIUS strain (>1010 CFU/g) and explored its effect on human gut microbiota. Methods: Forty-four volunteers completed the crossover intervention consisting of 2 months of ATECREM Ser...

title: Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 Attenuates Hyperoxia-Induced Lung Injury in a Newborn Rat Model.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a leading cause of morbidity in preterm infants, and effective preventive strategies are lacking. This study investigated the protective effect of orally administered Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 in a neonatal rat model of hyperoxia-induced lung injury. Methods: Newborn Sprague-Dawley rat pups were randomly allocated to normoxia control (NC), hyperoxia control (HC), and hyperoxia with probiotic supplementation (HP) groups. ...

title: The Screening and Identification of Potential Probiotics in Misgurnus anguillicaudatus Intestine.
abstract: We characterized the intestinal microbiota of Misgurnus anguillicaudatus using 16S rRNA gene sequencing (V4 region). Strains secreting extracellular digestive enzymes were functionally screened, identified by 16S rRNA sequencing, and evaluated for biosafety. Microbial diversity analysis revealed that the intestinal microbiota of M. anguillicaudatus was dominated by the genera Vibrio, Pseudoalteromonas, and Aeromonas as core predominant taxa. title: A randomized controlled double-blinded trial to assess the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus in non-anemic pregnant women who receive oral iron supplementation.
abstract: Pregnant women in India are routinely prescribed oral iron supplements as part of the national Anemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) program for anemia control. In women with iron-deficiency anemia, the benefits of iron supplementation during pregnancy, both for the mother and child, are very clear. In non-anemic pregnant women, however, the benefits of iron supplementation vis-à-vis associated risks that have been reported have not been studied adequately. Studies have suggested that iron may impair insulin...

title: Gastric microbiota‑derived postbiotics as antimicrobial and anti‑biofilm agents.
abstract: The human gastric microbiota is recognized as a diverse and metabolically active ecosystem with significant roles in health and disease. Beyond probiotics, postbiotics, non-viable microbial products with antimicrobial and anti-biofilm properties, offer stable and safer therapeutic alternatives. Rising antimicrobial resistance and biofilm associated infections caused by pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans highlight the urgent need for new strategies. title: AcmA-mediated non-GMO probiotic engineering for functional jujube juice fermentation.
abstract: Probiotics are indispensable functional microorganisms in food fermentation with increasingly promising application prospects. Although genetically modified probiotics show great potential in improving the quality of fermented foods, their practical application is hampered by ethical controversies and safety concerns. To address these issues, the sacB gene encoding levansucrase was cloned from Bacillus atrophaeus in this study. Three non-genetically modified (non-GMO) engineered strains were con...

title: Probiotics in type 1 diabetes: immunomodulatory mechanisms and the unresolved question of clinical efficacy.
abstract: Type 1 Diabetes (T1D) is a common autoimmune disease worldwide, which is associated with imbalanced gut microbiota. Intestinal dysbiosis plays a key role in the pathogenesis of T1D, and it may affect immune tolerance and autoimmune responses of pancreatic islet β-cells. As a potential immunomodulator, probiotics can help restore this balance, regulate immune responses, and reduce the risk of T1D. Although probiotics offer a logical immunomodulatory strategy to restore microbial and immune homeos...

title: Heat-Inactivated Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (RSB11) as a Multifunctional Postbiotic: Anti-Inflammatory Effects Compared with Live RSB11 Across Multiple Human Cell Models.
abstract: The clinical potential of probiotics is increasingly recognized; however, dependence on microbial viability, formulation and storage constraints, and safety considerations in vulnerable populations can limit their broader application. Postbiotics offer an alternative by providing inanimate microbial preparations with retained biological activity, yet whether heat inactivation preserves the functional effects of probiotic-derived candidates remains an important question. title: Prebiotic potential and modulation of the fecal microbiota by konjac oligo-glucomannan prepared using Pediococcus acidilactici mannanase.
abstract: In this study, konjac oligo-glucomannan (KOGM) was prepared from konjac glucomannan (KGM) by enzymatic hydrolysis using β-mannanase derived from Pediococcus acidilactici HDM2. The prepared KOGM had an average molecular weight of 13.4 kDa under optimized conditions (50 °C, pH 6.0, 80 U mL-1 and 180 min). title: In vitro assessment of the probiotic potential and safety of lactic acid bacteria for aquatic animal health.
abstract: This study evaluated the in vitro probiotic-related properties and preliminary safety profiles of five lactic acid bacteria (LAB) strains for potential use in aquaculture: Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATCC 55730, Lentilactobacillus kefiri K107, Latilactobacillus sakei SN34, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum FI8595, and Streptococcus thermophilus BioSt64. Probiotic-related traits included antimicrobial activity against Lactococcus garvieae and Yersinia ruckeri, aggregation-related properties, and tole...

title: Culture-free supernatant of potential probiotic Bacillus albus attenuates the expression of biofilm-associated virulence determinants in Burkholderia thailandensis and Staphylococcus aureus.
abstract: The role of native bacterial probiotics in the Chinese traditional fermentation starter, Qubing, has not been previously studied. In this investigation, 22 bacterial strains were isolated from Qubing, and potential probiotic candidates were selected for their antibiofilm activity against Burkholderia thailandensis and Staphylococcus aureus. title: C. butyricum Combined With Resmetirom Provides Therapeutic Benefits in MASH Associated With Gut-Liver-Brain Axis Modulation.
abstract: Resmetirom has emerged as a major advance in MASH pharmacotherapy as the first approved liver-targeted THR-β agonist; however, variable therapeutic efficacy and adverse responses may limit its clinical benefits. This study investigated whether C. butyricum could provide additional therapeutic benefits when combined with resmetirom and attenuate nausea/vomiting-like responses in association with changes across the gut-liver-brain axis.
journal: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

title: Effects of dietary supplementation with the antimicrobial peptide Sublancin on growth performance, antioxidant capacity, intestinal health, immune performance, and resistance to Aeromonas hydrophila in juvenile largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides).
abstract: A 56-day feeding trial was carried out to investigate how dietary Sublancin affects growth performance, antioxidative status, immune function, gut health, and disease resistance in largemouth bass. Five isonitrogenous and isocaloric experimental diets containing Sublancin at concentrations of 0 (Control), 100, 200, 400, and 800 mg/kg were formulated, which were respectively named Control, Sublancin 100, Sublancin 200, Sublancin 400, and Sublancin 800. title: Lactobacillus gasseri suppresses methionine-driven epigenetic programming of trained immunity-like priming to attenuate metabolic dysfunction.
abstract: Trained immunity-like epigenetic priming contributes to persistent metabolic inflammation in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but the upstream metabolic and microbiota-dependent regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. title: Probiotics attenuate AlCl₃-induced Alzheimer's disease via gut-brain axis modulation and suppression of NF-κB/NLRP3 neuroinflammation.
abstract: Disruptions along the brain-gut-microbiota axis significantly contribute to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis. This study evaluated the therapeutic potential of a multi-strain probiotic mixture in mitigating cognitive decline, neuroinflammation, and amyloid pathology in an AD rat model. In the present study, after induction of AD in rats by oral administration of AlCl3 (50 mg/kg) for 28 days, followed by oral treatment with a probiotic mixture (109 log CFU/ml) for 42 days. title: Effects of dietary supplements on lower-limb power and jump performance in physically active individuals and athletes: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
abstract: To evaluate the relative effects of dietary supplements, the certainty of evidence, and the robustness of findings within separate networks for peak power (PP), relative peak power (RPP), vertical jump (VJ), and countermovement jump (CMJ).
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: Protective effect of Glutamicibacter sp. ZY1 against Vibrio parahaemolyticus YDE17 pathogenicity in the clam Ruditapes philippinarum.
abstract: The use of probiotics is preferable to the use of antibiotics for the control of vibriosis. In this study, artificial infection showed that Glutamicibacter sp. ZY1 significantly protected the Manila clam Ruditapes philippinarum from infection by Vibrio parahaemolyticus YDE17, with a relative percent survival of 82.16%. Glutamicibacter sp. title: Comparative genomic and phenotypic profiling of commercial probiotic Enterococcus faecium strains: insights into safety and functional attributes.
abstract: Enterococcus faecium is widely used in probiotics but can also act as an opportunistic pathogen, necessitating strain-specific safety and efficacy assessments. While previous studies have characterized individual E. faecium probiotic strains, few have provided an integrated genomic and phenotypic comparison of multiple commercial strains from the Asian market. This study conducted a comparative genomic and phenotypic analysis of five E. faecium strains isolated from commercial probiotic products...

title: Supplementation of a Bacillus-based DFM mixture on growth performance, methane emissions, microbiome, and metabolome in backgrounding beef heifers.
abstract: Direct-fed microbials (DFM) have been used to improve livestock production efficiency and reduce environmental impact. Spore-forming bacteria such as Bacillus spp. present handling and processing advantages for use as a DFM; however, more information is needed about their effects in beef cattle. title: A Dominant Probiotic from the Traditional Chinese Fermented Food Douzhier Exhibits Anti-Influenza Activity.
abstract: Background: Douzhier, a traditional Chinese fermented food with a history spanning over 1000 years, harbors a complex community of beneficial microbiota. In this study, we isolated Lactococcus lactis subsp. cremoris (designated L. cremoris D2022), one of the dominant bacterial species in Douzhier, and evaluated its efficacy against influenza A virus (IAV) infection. title: Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-G101 Protects Against UVB-Induced Photoaging in HS68 Dermal Fibroblasts.
abstract: Background: Skin photoaging is primarily caused by prolonged ultraviolet (UV) exposure, which manifests as dryness and wrinkle formation. Recent studies highlight that beneficial microorganisms have garnered considerable attention for their emerging role in modulating host health, especially in skin photoaging. Methods: To investigate the role of two strains, Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis BL-G101 (BL-G101) and Lactobacillus acidophilus LA-G80 (LA-G80), in UVB-induced photoaging, we cond...

title: Effects of Acute Caffeine Supplementation on Performance and Physiological Responses in CrossFit: A Systematic Review and Three-Level Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Objectives: We quantified the influence of acute caffeine (CAF) supplementation on CrossFit performance and physiological outcomes and examined potential effect modifiers. Methods: Randomized crossover studies involving CAF supplementation in CrossFit were identified through systematic searches of multiple electronic databases. title: Dietary Fiber Supplementation Reduces Systolic Blood Pressure in High-Risk Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Hypertension: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Dietary fiber supplementation has been associated with blood pressure (BP) reduction, but evidence comparing soluble (SDF) and insoluble (IDF) fiber types in high-risk populations is limited. This study aimed to compare the effects of SDF and IDF supplementation on BP and to explore correlations between changes in BP and alterations in gut microbiota composition and serum biomarkers in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and hypertension. abstract: Background: Lepidium meyenii Walp. (maca) is a plant-derived feed supplement rich in bioactive compounds such as macamides, macaenes, glucosinolates, and polyphenols. In this study, it was selected as a potential natural functional feed additive based on its bioactive phytochemical composition, reported metabolic properties, and previously observed effects on porcine cells. title: Carbohydrate polymer-based nanoarmor systems for probiotic gastrointestinal delivery: Strategies, applications, and perspectives.
abstract: Probiotics have shown great potential for promoting human health. However, their viability is reduced during gastrointestinal transit owing to harsh conditions (e.g., gastric acidity, bile salts, and digestive enzymes). Recently, nanoarmor-based encapsulation has attracted extensive attention for probiotic protection and targeted delivery. title: A Novel GH26 β-Mannanase from Bacillus subtilis HM7 Producing Manno-Oligosaccharides with Strain-Specific Prebiotic Activity.
abstract: Mannan-oligosaccharide (MOS) produced from the hydrolysis of mannan by β-mannanase, demonstrate several beneficial properties, such as prebiotic and modulation of tight junction activity. In this study, two novel GH26 β-mannanases, MAN26HM7/A and MAN26HM7/B, from Bacillus subtilis HM7 were cloned and expressed in Escherichia coli BL21 (DE3). The optimal pH and temperature of MAN26HM7/A and MAN26HM7/B were pH 5.0 and 40 °C, and pH 6.0 and 60 °C, respectively. The β-mannanases from Bacillus subtil...

title: Effects of probiotic supplementation on inflammatory biomarkers in patients with depression: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Chronic low-grade inflammation has been widely acknowledged as an important pathophysiological mechanism underlying depression. Probiotics may alleviate depressive symptoms by modifying the microbiota-gut-brain axis and regulating inflammatory responses. The purpose of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to assess the effect of probiotic supplementation on circulating inflammatory biomarkers in depressed individuals.

title: Maternal and Embryonic Vitamin D3 Supplementation Improves Hepatic Lipid Metabolism in Progeny Chicks.
abstract: For oviparous laying hens, transition into the late-laying phase tends to be associated with reduced nutrient deposition in eggs. Accordingly, maternal dietary and in ovo supplementation of essential nutrients to eggs from late-phase hens could effectively improve embryonic development and even the subsequent performance of the offspring. title: A probiotic Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum converts hesperidin to bioactive hesperetin and improves metabolic dysfunction in aging mice.
abstract: Dietary flavonoids often require microbial metabolism to generate bioactive metabolites that influence host physiology. Hesperidin, a citrus flavanone glycoside, exhibits limited intestinal absorption and depends on gut microbial biotransformation to yield its active aglycone, hesperetin. Hesperetin activates CDGSH iron-sulfur domain 2 (CISD2), a pro-longevity gene whose expression declines with age, and its pharmacological activation has emerged as a strategy to promote healthy aging. title: Immunonutrition in weaning diets: Effect of Paecilomyces variotii (PEKILO®) on growth performance and health of gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata) larvae.
abstract: The replacement of fishmeal with sustainable microbial ingredients is a major challenge in marine larvi-culture, where nutritional quality and immune competence are critical during the weaning stage. This study evaluated the effects of dietary inclusion of Paecilomyces variotii (PEKILO®) mycoprotein in gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata) larvae. title: Intestinal Epithelial-Protective Effects of Leuconostoc mesenteroides H40 in LPS-Stimulated HT-29 Cells.
abstract: In this study, the intestinal epithelial-protective effects of Leuconostoc mesenteroides H40 (H40) were investigated using HT-29 intestinal epithelial cells. H40 reduced nitric oxide production in sodium nitroprusside (SNP)-treated cells and suppressed the lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced gene expression of inflammatory mediators, including interleukin-1 beta (IL-1β), IL-6, IL-8, TNF-α, and COX-2. abstract: Brain aging is a major contributor to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disorders. Ferroptosis, a regulated form of cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation, has emerged as a key mechanism associated with age-related hippocampal dysfunction. Here, we investigated whether dietary supplementation of Magnolia kobus DC. abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the levels of muscle appearance satisfaction and ergogenic aid use among adult male amateur bodybuilders.
journal: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association

abstract: Male fertility supplements reduce oxidative stress, but whether they improve fertility is controversial. title: [Observation of the impact of nutritional support with beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate on lean mass parameters of body composition in patients with obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus and metabolically associated fatty liver disease].
abstract: Sarcopenic obesity is closely related to the occurrence of metabolically associated fatty liver disease (MASLD), but the factors that influence the effectiveness of dietary supplements in increasing muscle mass have not yet been clarified.

abstract: The microbiota comprises communities of microorganisms that establish complex relationships with the host and play key roles in physiology, metabolism, and immunity. Increasing evidence highlights microbiota alterations in several diseases, particularly those driven by oxidative stress-induced inflammation. abstract: Nutritional deficiencies and parasitic infections continue to undermine immune defenses and drive anemia rates among adolescents, creating a significant public health challenge in sub-Saharan Africa. Although multiple factors contribute to this burden, the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency (ID) remain the most critical levers for progress. abstract: Despite growing interest in starch-lipid complexes as prebiotic ingredients, the impact of fatty acid (FA) unsaturation on their fermentative behavior and gut microbiota modulation remains controversial, largely due to inconsistent structural characterization across studies. abstract: In this study, 49 intestinal bacterial isolates were recovered from healthy Micropterus salmoides, among which five candidate Bacillus subtilis strains were screened via multi-index in vitro evaluation. An 8-week feeding trial covering six treatment groups was conducted to assess growth performance and survival upon Edwardsiella piscicida immersion challenge. abstract: Background/Objectives: Sarcopenia is an age-associated skeletal muscle disorder that may be aggravated by a high-fat diet (HFD). Given the multifactorial pathogenesis of sarcopenia, single-nutrient interventions may be insufficient. This study investigated whether a specialized multinutrient formula could attenuate muscle dysfunction and intramuscular lipid accumulation in adult mice under standard-diet and HFD-fed conditions. abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a pervasive global health crisis, with type 2 diabetes (T2D) representing the majority of cases.
